# Lab 4 - published checks (Tier A)

These are the checks `itsmlab verify 4` runs; the grader runs the same checker on the receipted commit
and then opens the sealed fault in your snapshot for the two checks only it can make (4.06, 5.06; shown
as `skip` locally). Bundles: **Core** is pass/fail as a whole, **Stretch** passes at any two of three, and
the postmortem's narrative is read by the lecturer. Ids are stable; every rule id (`I-nn`) is defined in
`INCIDENT-SPEC.md`.

Nothing of the playground runs on the grader: the incident happened on your machine, and everything is
recomputed from the two artifacts you ship, `incident/tsdb-snapshot.tar.gz` and `incident/ticket.json`,
with the checker's own Prometheus, Alertmanager 0.34.1 and amtool. `itsmlab incident 4` prints the same
recomputation. Messages never name the seeded flags.

|---|---|---|
| L4-CORE-1.01 | compose file defines service svcdesk with build | a compose file at the repo root defines a service `svcdesk` with a `build:` key |
| L4-CORE-1.02 | no host-path bind mounts on svcdesk | in the resolved configuration `svcdesk` has no host-path bind mount |
| L4-CORE-1.03 | compose up --wait svcdesk within 120 s | after an untimed `docker compose build`, `docker compose up --wait svcdesk` succeeds within 120 s |

## L4-CORE-3 `incident` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L4-CORE-3.01 | the snapshot loads | `incident/tsdb-snapshot.tar.gz` exists, is at most 50 MB, holds Prometheus blocks, and the checker's Prometheus serves them |

| L4-CORE-3.05 | the detecting alert resolved in the snapshot | the detecting alert's firing run ends before the snapshot does |
| L4-CORE-3.06 | the P1 ticket | `incident/ticket.json`: priority P1, created at or after the onset, acknowledged not before detection |
| L4-CORE-3.07 | the acknowledgement is in svcdesk's telemetry | the snapshot shows a successful POST on `/tickets/{...}/ack` from 15 s before to 20 s after `acknowledged_at`, and a successful POST /tickets around `created_at` |
| L4-CORE-3.08 | the page reached the pager | `itsm_pager_notifications_total{receiver="pager",status="firing"}` rose after the onset |
| L4-CORE-3.09 | the postmortem's clocks match the recomputation | the four instants and MTTD, MTTA, MTTR in the postmortem's front matter are within 30 s of what the checker recomputes (MTTD = detection - onset, MTTA = acknowledgement - detection, MTTR = recovery - onset), and `detecting_alert` is the recomputed detecting alert's name |
